description.summary: the compositor types a stored secret for the secrets daemon

protocol.description:
The CrownOS secrets daemon (crownos-secretsd) keeps passwords and API keys that AI agents may use by name without ever reading the value. When an agent asks to type a secret into a field, the daemon hands the value to the compositor through this protocol, and the compositor types it. The value never passes through the agent, the accessibility bus or the clipboard.
Only crownos-secretsd may bind the manager global: the compositor checks the executable behind the client when it connects (for example exe:/usr/bin/crownos-secretsd, a Spawned or HostExecutable key) and must not advertise the global to any other client. The daemon connects before it turns off PR_SET_DUMPABLE, so the compositor can read who it is.
For each type_secret request the compositor must:
- show its own confirmation that names the agent, the secret, the window and the origin. The compositor draws it itself, outside every client, and ignores synthetic input on it (input from crownos_input, virtual keyboards, agent cursors or driven seats). The daemon has asked the user already when its rules say so; this second question is the one that no client can fake. A compositor may skip it only when the daemon passed the confirmed flag and its own policy allows that. - check that the keyboard focus is on a surface of the given window, and, when require_password_field is set, that the focused text_input_v3 has the content purpose password. Otherwise it answers focus_changed or not_password_field and types nothing. - refuse a terminal emulator (a window whose app id the compositor knows as a terminal): text typed there is a command line. It answers refused. - flag the window sensitive before the first key, and keep the flag for 30 seconds after the last one, so screenshots, screencasts and the context engine do not see the field while it fills. - inject the text through the text_input_v3 commit of the focused client, or, when the client has no text input, as key events on the user's seat. It types nothing that is not in the value. - zero its copy of the value as soon as it is typed or refused, and never log it or send it to any other client.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_secret_input_manager_v1

description.summary: types secrets into windows for crownos-secretsd

interface.description: A global for crownos-secretsd only. Each request names its own id; the compositor answers each with one done event.

entry.name: duplicate_id
entry.summary: an id that is still open was used again

entry.name: bad_value
entry.summary: the value fd is not a readable sealed memfd or pipe

entry.name: tab_after
entry.summary: press Tab after the value, to the next field

entry.name: confirmed
entry.summary: the user already allowed this use in the daemon's dialog

entry.name: focus_changed
entry.summary: the focus was not on the given window

entry.name: not_password_field
entry.summary: the focused field is not a password field

entry.name: refused
entry.summary: the compositor refused, for example a terminal

entry.name: cancelled
entry.summary: the user said no in the compositor's confirmation

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Open requests end with done(cancelled).

request.name: type_secret

description.summary: type a value into the focused field of a window

request.description:
Asks the compositor to type the value in fd into the field that has the keyboard focus in the given window, after the checks above.
The fd is a memfd sealed against writes, growing and shrinking, or the read end of a pipe whose write end the daemon closed. It holds the value as UTF-8, at most 32768 bytes. The compositor reads it once, closes it, and zeroes what it read after use.
The agent, secret_name and origin strings are only for the compositor's confirmation; origin is empty when there is none and is a hint that the compositor checks again where it can.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: chosen by the daemon, unique while open

arg.name: require_password_field
arg.summary: 1 to type only into a password field

arg.name: agent
arg.summary: the agent's app key, for the confirmation

arg.name: secret_name
arg.summary: the secret's key name, for the confirmation

event.name: done

description.summary: the outcome of a type_secret request

event.description: Sent once for each type_secret request; the id is free again after it.
